targetTexts.1: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
targetTexts.2: Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
targetTexts.3: Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?
targetTexts.4: Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?
targetTexts.5: Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?
targetTexts.6: Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?
targetTexts.7: Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
targetTexts.8: If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!
targetTexts.9: Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?
targetTexts.10: No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?
targetTexts.11: Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
targetTexts.12: I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.
targetTexts.13: Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
targetTexts.14: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
targetTexts.15: His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.
targetTexts.16: One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.
targetTexts.17: They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.
targetTexts.18: His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
targetTexts.19: Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!
targetTexts.20: Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
targetTexts.21: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
targetTexts.22: Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
targetTexts.23: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
targetTexts.24: His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!
targetTexts.25: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.
targetTexts.26: The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.
targetTexts.27: He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
targetTexts.28: No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
targetTexts.29: A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.
targetTexts.30: His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.
targetTexts.31: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
targetTexts.32: He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!
targetTexts.33: Nothing on earth is his equal—a creature devoid of fear!
targetTexts.34: He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”
